cases.target_rule: A trait method is available through method-call syntax only when the trait participates in method lookup at the call site.
cases.intended_cause: The `Words` trait is imported before the call, so method lookup can consider its implementation for `str` and resolve `"a b".words()` without changing the receiver type.
cases.principled_repair: Keep the import near the consumer.
cases.weak_repair: Replace method syntax with unrelated code.

cases.target_rule: A generic body may use trait behavior only when the function signature promises that every admissible type parameter implements that trait.
cases.intended_cause: The body calls `label()` on unconstrained `T`, but callers are currently allowed to choose a type with no `Label` implementation. Rust therefore rejects the body while checking the generic definition, before any call exists.
cases.weak_repair: Make the function accept only one concrete type without reviewing the API.

cases.target_rule: An implementation inherits a trait default method when it supplies every required item used by that default.
cases.intended_cause: `User` implements the required `name` method, so the inherited `greeting` body has all of the behavior it needs and is callable without an override.
cases.weak_repair: Override every implementation without semantic need.

cases.target_rule: Receiver syntax cannot choose between multiple equally applicable trait methods with the same name and receiver type.
cases.intended_cause: Both `A::id` and `B::id` are implemented for `X`; `x.id()` supplies no information that selects one contract, so fully qualified syntax is required.
cases.principled_repair: Use fully qualified syntax to select the contract.
cases.weak_repair: Rename methods arbitrarily without reviewing semantics.

cases.target_rule: A method guarded by `where Self: Sized` is excluded from the trait-object dispatch surface while remaining available to concrete implementors.
cases.intended_cause: `name` has an object-callable receiver and can be used through `&dyn Named`; `boxed` is invoked only on concrete `X`, where the compiler knows its size and can construct `Box<Self>`.
cases.weak_repair: Remove the trait-object use entirely.

cases.target_rule: Implementing a trait also requires satisfying every supertrait named in its declaration.
cases.intended_cause: `Audit` promises that every implementor is also an `Id`, yet `X` has no `Id` implementation. The default `audit` method cannot rely on `self.id()` until that prerequisite is real.
cases.principled_repair: Implement the real prerequisite or remove an unjustified supertrait.
cases.weak_repair: Add an empty prerequisite implementation with no valid semantics.

cases.target_rule: A bounded implementation exists only for concrete substitutions that satisfy its declared bounds.
cases.intended_cause: `Wrapped<T>` implements `Render` only when `T: Render`; the chosen `T = u8` has that implementation, so the delegated call is legal.
cases.weak_repair: Clone or stringify without the contract.

cases.target_rule: Calling a method whose receiver is `self` moves a non-`Copy` receiver into that call.
cases.intended_cause: `finish` consumes the `String`; the later formatting expression tries to use the same moved value, so ownership has already ended at the method call.
cases.principled_repair: Use the returned value or redesign the receiver if consumption is not semantic.
cases.weak_repair: Clone before every call without ownership justification.

cases.target_rule: For a fixed trait implementation, an associated type projection is uniquely determined by the implementor.
cases.intended_cause: `S: Source` fixes `S::Item` to `u8`; therefore `T::Item` in `first` is a well-formed return type and `s.get()` produces exactly that projection.
cases.weak_repair: Add an unrelated generic type parameter.

cases.target_rule: When several traits define an associated item with the same name, the projection must identify the owning trait.
cases.intended_cause: `X` implements both `A` and `B`, and each supplies a different `Item`; `X::Item` omits the trait path, so the compiler cannot know whether the intended type is `u8` or `u16`.
cases.principled_repair: Use `<X as A>::Item` or `<X as B>::Item`.
cases.weak_repair: Rename associated items only to silence one call.

cases.target_rule: A trait type parameter permits one implementor to participate in distinct implementations for different parameter values.
cases.intended_cause: `Bytes` implements `Convert<Vec<u8>>` and `Convert<String>` as separate relationships. The expected result type at each assignment selects the corresponding implementation.
cases.weak_repair: Replace both outputs with strings.

cases.target_rule: A type may provide only one implementation of a trait, and that implementation fixes each associated type once.
cases.intended_cause: The two `Source for S` implementations overlap completely and attempt to assign two incompatible meanings to `Source::Item`; coherence rejects the second implementation.
cases.principled_repair: Use a generic trait parameter if multiple relationships are real.
cases.weak_repair: Wrap arbitrary branches in `Box<dyn Any>`.

cases.target_rule: A generic associated type may produce a family of types indexed by the lifetime of each borrow.
cases.intended_cause: `Text::Out<'a>` is `&'a str`, and `view` returns a slice whose lifetime is tied to the particular borrow of `self` rather than to one global associated type.
cases.weak_repair: Return owned strings without considering the requirement.

cases.target_rule: A value returned from a lending method may keep the mutable borrow of the lender active until that value is last used.
cases.intended_cause: `a` borrows from `s` through the first `next`; the second call needs another mutable borrow of `s` while `a` is still used later, so the two loans overlap.
cases.principled_repair: Finish using or drop the first view before advancing.
cases.weak_repair: Clone all source state without requirement evidence.

cases.target_rule: A trait object with associated types must fix those associated types so its erased method signatures are complete.
cases.intended_cause: `dyn Source` leaves `Source::Item` unknown, so the return type of `get` cannot be represented as one object-safe callable signature. The object type must state an equality such as `Item = u8` or remain generic.
cases.principled_repair: Write `dyn Source<Item = u8>` or use a generic boundary.
cases.weak_repair: Erase outputs into strings.

cases.target_rule: A trait whose dispatch surface depends on a generic associated type is not dyn-compatible under the current object model.
cases.intended_cause: The erased object would need to represent the lifetime-indexed family `Item<'a>` for arbitrary caller borrows, but one vtable method signature cannot encode that family here.
cases.principled_repair: Keep static dispatch or define a separate dyn-compatible adapter.
cases.weak_repair: Delete borrowing semantics from the core trait without review.

cases.target_rule: A crate may implement a trait it owns for a type it does not own.
cases.intended_cause: Because `Words` is local, this crate is the coherence authority for its implementations and may lawfully implement it for the foreign type `str`.
cases.weak_repair: Create a wrapper when no distinct semantics exist.

cases.target_rule: A crate may implement a foreign trait for a type it owns.
cases.intended_cause: `Local` is defined in this crate, so the orphan rules permit a `Display` implementation even though `Display` comes from the standard library.
cases.weak_repair: Use a type alias and expect new ownership.

cases.target_rule: The orphan rules prohibit implementing a foreign trait for a foreign type when the current crate owns neither side of the relationship.
cases.intended_cause: Both `Display` and `Vec<u8>` are defined elsewhere; accepting this implementation would let unrelated crates create conflicting global meanings for the same pair.
cases.weak_repair: Use a type alias, which does not create a new type.

cases.target_rule: Two implementations are illegal when some possible type could satisfy both implementation heads.
cases.intended_cause: A type may implement both `A` and `B`, so the two blanket implementations could both claim `Mark` for the same type. Rust rejects the overlap even if no such concrete type is written yet.
cases.principled_repair: Use disjoint wrapper types or explicit dispatch.
cases.weak_repair: Wait for specialization or add arbitrary marker exclusions.

cases.target_rule: A local newtype creates a distinct nominal type and gives the current crate coherence ownership over foreign-trait implementations for it.
cases.intended_cause: `Hex` is not an alias for `Vec<u8>`; it is a new local type, so its `Display` implementation is legal and can express hexadecimal semantics without changing `Vec` globally.
cases.weak_repair: Implement Deref solely to expose every inner method.

cases.target_rule: Extension methods participate in receiver syntax only while their trait is in scope.
cases.intended_cause: The implementation for `str` exists, but `ext::X` is not imported at the call site, so method lookup does not consider `X::x`.
cases.principled_repair: Import the extension trait or use qualified syntax.
cases.weak_repair: Add an inherent method to a type you do not own.

cases.target_rule: A public trait sealed by a private supertrait can be implemented only by types for which the defining crate supplies the private prerequisite.
cases.intended_cause: `Mine` cannot implement the inaccessible `private::Sealed` trait, so it cannot satisfy the supertrait contract required by `api::Token`.
cases.principled_repair: Use supported implementors or an exposed adapter.
cases.weak_repair: Make the private trait public only to silence the error.

cases.target_rule: A type alias introduces another name, not a new nominal type or a new coherence identity.
cases.intended_cause: `Bytes` and `Vec<u8>` are the same type, so the second `Mark` implementation duplicates the first instead of defining a separate relationship.
cases.principled_repair: Use a newtype for a distinct relationship.
cases.weak_repair: Rename the alias again.

cases.target_rule: A method body may use formatting only when the method or enclosing implementation constrains the field type with the required formatting trait.
cases.intended_cause: `format!("{}", self.0)` requires `T: Display`, but the unconstrained implementation promises `show` for every `T`; generic checking therefore rejects the body.
cases.principled_repair: Put the bound on the method or a separate impl block.
cases.weak_repair: Put every possible bound on the struct.

cases.target_rule: Bounds can be placed on only the methods or implementation blocks that require them, leaving unrelated capabilities available to more types.
cases.intended_cause: `first` is available for every `Pair<T>`, while `max` is available only when `T: PartialOrd`; the `i32` pair satisfies the narrower comparison contract.
cases.weak_repair: Constrain the entire struct.

cases.target_rule: Separate argument-position `impl Trait` occurrences denote independent hidden type parameters unless the signature explicitly ties them together.
cases.intended_cause: `a` and `b` need only implement `Display`; one may be an integer and the other a string slice because no equality relation is declared between their concrete types.
cases.weak_repair: Assume the types are equal in the body.

cases.target_rule: Reusing one named type parameter for two arguments requires both arguments to have exactly the same concrete type.
cases.intended_cause: `show<T>(_: T, _: T)` cannot choose one `T` that is simultaneously `u8` and `u16`; independent parameters are needed when equality is not part of the contract.
cases.principled_repair: Use separate type parameters when equality is unnecessary.
cases.weak_repair: Convert both values to String regardless of semantics.

cases.target_rule: Every return path of one return-position `impl Trait` function must produce the same hidden concrete type.
cases.intended_cause: The `if` branches produce `u8` and `&str`. Both implement `Display`, but the opaque return denotes one concrete type, not a run-time union of all implementors.
cases.principled_repair: Use an enum, trait object, or one unified concrete adapter.
cases.weak_repair: Return formatted strings solely to erase differences.

cases.target_rule: A return-position `impl Trait` hides a single concrete return type from callers while preserving its stated capabilities for static dispatch.
cases.intended_cause: The function always returns the same array iterator type and promises `Iterator<Item = u8>`, so callers may use iterator methods without learning the concrete name.
cases.weak_repair: Expose a long concrete iterator type publicly.

cases.target_rule: Callers of an opaque return may rely only on bounds named in the public return type.
cases.intended_cause: Although the hidden value happens to be a `String`, the signature promises only `Display`; `clone` is therefore unavailable until `Clone` becomes an intentional part of the contract.
cases.principled_repair: Add a justified Clone bound or avoid requiring it.
cases.weak_repair: Downcast the opaque value.

cases.target_rule: A consuming generic method may return the same structure instantiated with a different type parameter.
cases.intended_cause: `map` owns the original pair, preserves its first field, and returns `P<A, C>`; the annotated result exactly matches the new `C = &str` state.
cases.weak_repair: Hide all strategy changes behind dynamic dispatch.

cases.target_rule: A trait object type is written explicitly with `dyn` and may dispatch only methods represented by the object-safe trait surface.
cases.intended_cause: `&dyn Name` erases the concrete `X` while retaining the callable `name(&self) -> &str` contract, so `show` can dispatch through the object.
cases.weak_repair: Make the function generic when runtime erasure is required.

cases.target_rule: A trait method with its own unconstrained type parameter cannot be represented by one finite vtable entry for a trait object.
cases.intended_cause: `encode<T>` asks each call site to choose an arbitrary `T`; after erasing the concrete implementor, `dyn Encode` has no single monomorphic method signature to dispatch.
cases.principled_repair: Move it to a Sized extension or erase the parameter.
cases.weak_repair: Replace the result with String and ignore semantics.

cases.target_rule: A trait-object method cannot return bare `Self` because the erased concrete return type and its size are unknown to the caller.
cases.intended_cause: `copy_like` promises the implementing type itself, but `dyn CopyLike` deliberately hides that type; the object interface therefore cannot describe the returned value.
cases.principled_repair: Mark the method Self:Sized or define a boxed clone contract.
cases.weak_repair: Return `Box<dyn Any>`.

cases.target_rule: An associated constant has no receiver and is selected through a concrete implementation, so it is not a dispatchable trait-object member.
cases.intended_cause: `dyn Meta` cannot choose `Meta::NAME` through a vtable receiver. Dynamic metadata must be exposed by an object-callable method or separated from the erased interface.
cases.principled_repair: Move dynamic metadata to a method or split a static metadata trait.
cases.weak_repair: Hard-code the value in callers.

cases.target_rule: A trait object must specify associated types that occur in its callable method signatures.
cases.intended_cause: `Box<dyn Source>` leaves the return type of `get` unknown; an equality such as `dyn Source<Item = u8>` is required to make the erased interface complete.
cases.principled_repair: Use `dyn Source<Item=u8>` or a generic boundary.
cases.weak_repair: Erase the item into String.

cases.target_rule: A concrete-only method guarded by `Self: Sized` may construct a trait object without making that method part of the object dispatch surface.
cases.intended_cause: `X.boxed()` runs while `Self` is known and sized, returning `Box<dyn Name>`; subsequent calls use only the object-safe `name` method.
cases.weak_repair: Remove useful constructor convenience entirely.

cases.target_rule: A trait object may contain borrowed data when its object lifetime is tied explicitly to the source borrow.
cases.intended_cause: `Box<dyn Name + 'a>` records that the erased `Borrowed<'a>` object cannot outlive `s`; no unnecessary `'static` requirement is introduced.
cases.weak_repair: Require static data unnecessarily.

cases.target_rule: Owned trait objects allow values of different concrete types to coexist when they share one sufficient dyn-compatible contract.
cases.intended_cause: `Box<A>` and `Box<B>` are coerced to `Box<dyn N>`; the vector stores one erased pointer representation and dispatches `n` through each value’s vtable.
cases.weak_repair: Downcast each value for ordinary execution.

cases.target_rule: Private fields plus a validating constructor can make every externally constructible value satisfy a domain invariant.
cases.intended_cause: Callers cannot write the inner byte directly; `Percent::new` is the authority that admits only values at most 100, and `get` exposes observation without reopening construction.
cases.weak_repair: Expose the field and rely on callers.

cases.target_rule: A public tuple struct with a private field cannot be constructed outside its defining module.
cases.intended_cause: `m::Percent(200)` attempts to bypass the module’s construction authority, but the private field keeps the representation and its invariant inaccessible.
cases.weak_repair: Make the field public.

cases.target_rule: A wrapper may delegate behavior only for inner types that satisfy the delegated trait contract.
cases.intended_cause: `Signed<T>` implements `R` under `T: R`; the concrete inner `&str` satisfies that bound, so the wrapper can call `self.0.r()` and add its own behavior.
cases.weak_repair: Implement unrelated capabilities blindly.

cases.target_rule: A directly recursive field requires indirection because a value cannot contain another complete value of the same type inline.
cases.intended_cause: `Decorator { inner: Decorator }` has no finite size: determining its size requires determining itself again. A pointer-like indirection or nonrecursive representation must break the cycle.
cases.principled_repair: Add indirection or use a nonrecursive composition.
cases.weak_repair: Use Rc without shared ownership need.

cases.target_rule: An enum represents a closed set of variants that can be handled exhaustively with direct pattern matching.
cases.intended_cause: `run` covers both `Add` and `Clear`, so every possible `C` value has a defined branch and no dynamic registry is required.
cases.weak_repair: Replace with trait objects absent extension needs.

cases.target_rule: A match over a locally known enum must cover every variant unless an explicit fallback handles the remainder.
cases.intended_cause: `Published` has no arm, so `code` is not total over `State`; the compiler rejects a function that could receive an unhandled value.
cases.principled_repair: Add meaningful handling for the state.
cases.weak_repair: Use a wildcard that hides future semantics.

cases.target_rule: Delegated behavior is available only when the composed inner type satisfies the wrapper implementation’s trait bound.
cases.intended_cause: `D<T>: R` exists only for `T: R`; `X` has no `R` implementation, so `D(X)` does not have the delegated `r` method.
cases.principled_repair: Use an inner type satisfying the contract or remove invalid delegation.
cases.weak_repair: Add an empty implementation with false semantics.

cases.target_rule: A generic bound `A + B` requires one concrete value to satisfy both capability contracts simultaneously.
cases.intended_cause: `X` implements both traits, so `sum` may call `a` and `b` through the same borrowed value and combine their results.
cases.weak_repair: Create a nominal supertrait with no new law.

cases.target_rule: A consuming transition may change the type parameter that represents protocol state.
cases.intended_cause: `review` consumes `Doc<Draft>` and returns `Doc<Reviewed>`; the annotated result confirms that the old state cannot remain available after the transition.
cases.weak_repair: Store a boolean alongside the marker.

cases.target_rule: Methods implemented only for one typestate are absent from all other typestate instantiations.
cases.intended_cause: `publish` exists for `Doc<Reviewed>` but the value is `Doc<Draft>`; method lookup correctly reports that the required transition has not occurred.
cases.weak_repair: Add publish to every state and return unsupported errors.

cases.target_rule: Private marker fields prevent callers from forging privileged typestates directly.
cases.intended_cause: `Reviewed(())` requires access to its private field, so external code cannot manufacture the state that unlocks `publish`; it must use an authorized transition.
cases.weak_repair: Expose marker fields.

cases.target_rule: A transition taking `self` moves the old-state value and makes only the returned new-state value available.
cases.intended_cause: `x.go()` consumes `x`; trying to bind `_z = x` afterward would preserve two protocol states for one resource, so ownership rejects it.
cases.principled_repair: Use the returned state or preserve ownership in an error type.
cases.weak_repair: Clone the full object before every transition.

cases.target_rule: An owned capability token is linear unless it implements a duplication mechanism such as `Copy` or `Clone`.
cases.intended_cause: The first `use_it(p)` consumes `p`; the second call attempts to reuse an authorization that has already been spent.
cases.principled_repair: Issue a new authorized permit if policy allows.
cases.weak_repair: Make the permit Copy and destroy single-use semantics.

cases.target_rule: A typestate builder exposes `build` only for the instantiation in which all required components are present.
cases.intended_cause: `B::new()` produces `B<M, M>`, while `build` exists only for `B<P<S>, P<u8>>`; the method set records the missing configuration at compile time.
cases.weak_repair: Add a build method that panics at runtime.

cases.target_rule: A closed enum can erase several typestate instantiations into one run-time value when later code must handle all states explicitly.
cases.intended_cause: `Any` stores either `X<D>` or `X<R>`, and the exhaustive match recovers the state distinction without pretending both variants share the same methods.
cases.weak_repair: Erase all state into unvalidated strings.

cases.target_rule: A public generic state parameter can remain extension-controlled when its trait is sealed by a private prerequisite.
cases.intended_cause: Only the defining module can implement the private state trait, so external code cannot invent unsupported state types for `X<T>`.
cases.weak_repair: Make arbitrary state parameters legal.

cases.target_rule: A blanket extension implementation can add a method to every type satisfying the extension trait’s prerequisite bounds.
cases.intended_cause: `impl<T: Display + ?Sized> Ext for T` includes `str`, so the borrowed string receives `bracket` while the method remains derived from `Display`.
cases.weak_repair: Put every convenience method in the core trait.

cases.target_rule: An extension trait must be in scope before its methods participate in receiver-style lookup.
cases.intended_cause: `u8` implements `x::Ext`, but the trait is not imported in `main`; the method therefore remains invisible despite the existing implementation.
cases.weak_repair: Copy the method as a free function at every call.

cases.target_rule: A closure that mutates captured state implements `FnMut`, not the stronger repeatable shared-call contract `Fn`.
cases.intended_cause: The closure increments `n`, requiring mutable access to its capture. `twice` promises to call through an immutable callable interface, so its bound is too strong for this closure.
cases.principled_repair: Accept FnMut with mutable receiver or remove mutation.
cases.weak_repair: Use RefCell solely to satisfy Fn.

cases.target_rule: `TryFrom` expresses a fallible conversion that may establish a stronger validated target invariant.
cases.intended_cause: `P::try_from` rejects values above 100 and constructs the private wrapper only for admitted bytes, so both the failure and success paths preserve the percentage contract.
cases.weak_repair: Implement From and panic on invalid input.

cases.target_rule: A generic port may bind each implementation to its own associated error type while propagating that type through callers.
cases.intended_cause: `run<T: S>` returns `Result<u8, T::E>`; for `M`, the projection is `Infallible`, so the generic boundary preserves the implementation-specific error family without erasure.
cases.weak_repair: Convert every error to String at the trait boundary.

cases.target_rule: A trait object must fix associated types that appear in object-callable method signatures.
cases.intended_cause: `Box<dyn S>` leaves `S::E` unspecified, so the erased return type `Result<u8, Self::E>` is incomplete. The object must constrain `E` or the boundary must remain generic.
cases.principled_repair: Fix the error type or keep the port generic.
cases.weak_repair: Erase errors into strings without preserving sources.

cases.target_rule: A fake is useful when it implements the same behavioral port and can deliberately exercise success and failure semantics.
cases.intended_cause: `Fake(true)` returns the port’s declared error rather than bypassing the contract, so the test observes a real boundary behavior through the same interface.
cases.weak_repair: Add test-only controls to the production trait.

cases.target_rule: A generic function must declare every trait capability used by its body.
cases.intended_cause: `run` calls `load` on unconstrained `T`; because the signature does not promise `T: S`, the method is unavailable while the generic body is checked.
cases.weak_repair: Make the function accept only the fake.

cases.target_rule: Adding a required method to a public trait invalidates existing implementations that cannot supply the new item.
cases.intended_cause: `Old` implements the previous `run` contract but omits the newly required `id`; the compiler exposes the downstream implementation break immediately.
cases.principled_repair: Use a major version, defensible default, or new trait.
cases.weak_repair: Add a meaningless empty implementation.

cases.target_rule: When two imported traits provide the same applicable method name, receiver syntax becomes ambiguous even if both methods have defaults.
cases.intended_cause: `X` implements both `A` and `B`; `X.name()` does not select which default is intended, so qualification or a redesigned extension surface is required.
cases.weak_repair: Rely on import order.

cases.target_rule: Adding a supertrait strengthens the implementation contract for every existing implementor.
cases.intended_cause: `P: Id` now requires `Old` to implement `Id` before its `P` implementation is valid; this is a downstream breaking change, not a free refactor.
cases.principled_repair: Make a major change or separate extension trait.
cases.weak_repair: Add false prerequisite implementations.

cases.target_rule: A new blanket implementation can overlap with a downstream explicit implementation for a type that satisfies the blanket bound.
cases.intended_cause: `Local: Display` makes the blanket `impl<T: Display> P for T` apply, while the explicit `impl P for Local` claims the same pair; coherence rejects the conflict.
cases.principled_repair: Use an adapter newtype or avoid the blanket impl.
cases.weak_repair: Delete downstream semantics.

cases.target_rule: A sealed trait limits the set of implementors, allowing the defining crate to evolve implementation obligations without breaking third-party implementations.
cases.intended_cause: Only `api` can satisfy the private prerequisite for `T`; `X` is an authorized implementor and downstream crates are consumers rather than uncontrolled implementors.
cases.weak_repair: Promise downstream implementation accidentally.

cases.target_rule: A non-exhaustive public enum requires downstream matches to include a fallback for variants that may be added later.
cases.intended_cause: `std::io::ErrorKind` is non-exhaustive; matching only two known variants would make downstream code source-incompatible with future additions, so a wildcard or equivalent fallback is mandatory.
cases.weak_repair: Assume no variants will be added.

cases.target_rule: An adapter can preserve an old contract while presenting a newer interface with added metadata or failure structure.
cases.intended_cause: `A<T>` delegates `V1::run`, supplies the new identifier, and lifts the infallible old result into `Result`, allowing old behavior to participate in the V2 boundary.
cases.weak_repair: Pretend a required V2 semantic can be defaulted.

cases.target_rule: Adding a trait bound excludes callers whose types previously satisfied the public function signature.
cases.intended_cause: `use_it` now requires `Clone`, but `NotClone` lacks that capability; the call demonstrates the source break caused by strengthening a generic requirement.
cases.principled_repair: Treat the stronger requirement as breaking or move it to the specific method.
cases.weak_repair: Implement meaningless Clone solely for compatibility.

cases.target_rule: A design may keep stable outer boundaries generic while storing runtime-variable behavior behind trait objects.
cases.intended_cause: `run` monomorphizes the `Source` boundary for `M` and iterates a heterogeneous slice of `Box<dyn R>` for rules, using each dispatch mechanism where its variation is real.
cases.weak_repair: Erase every boundary for uniform appearance.

cases.target_rule: An associated-type equality at an engine boundary is a real requirement that every source implementation must satisfy.
cases.intended_cause: `run` requires `S<Item = u8>`, but `X::Item` is `String`; the mismatch is rejected before the engine can index or return an assumed byte.
cases.principled_repair: Constrain the associated type at the engine boundary.
cases.weak_repair: Convert arbitrary items to strings.

cases.target_rule: A runtime registry requires a dyn-compatible execution trait whose methods have fixed erased signatures.
cases.intended_cause: `Rule::run<T>` is generic over a caller-selected type, so `Box<dyn Rule>` cannot form a finite vtable entry for that method. Static construction and dynamic execution must be separated.
cases.principled_repair: Split static construction from dyn execution.
cases.weak_repair: Make all input String.

cases.target_rule: A typestate builder may expose `build` only after every required component is represented in its type parameters.
cases.intended_cause: `B::new()` is still `B<M, M>`; the only `build` implementation belongs to `B<P<S>, P<u8>>`, so the incomplete architecture cannot be constructed.
cases.weak_repair: Add a runtime panic in build.

cases.target_rule: A foreign trait cannot be implemented directly for a foreign collection type; a local semantic adapter must own the relationship.
cases.intended_cause: Both `Display` and `Vec<String>` are foreign, so this crate lacks coherence authority. A local newtype can provide formatting without claiming a global meaning for all vectors.
cases.weak_repair: Use a type alias.

cases.target_rule: An opaque iterator return can hide the concrete adapter chain while preserving a borrowed item type and static dispatch.
cases.intended_cause: `errors` always returns one concrete filtering iterator over `&u8`; callers see only `Iterator<Item = &u8>` and cannot depend on the internal chain.
cases.weak_repair: Box the iterator without runtime need.

cases.target_rule: A storage boundary requiring `T: 'static` rejects values that contain references to shorter-lived local data.
cases.intended_cause: `B(&s)` borrows the local `String`, so it cannot satisfy the registry’s `'static` requirement. The registry must carry a lifetime or own the referenced data.
cases.principled_repair: Give the registry an explicit lifetime or own the data.
cases.weak_repair: Leak the borrowed string.

cases.target_rule: A sealed built-in marker intentionally prevents downstream types from joining the privileged built-in set while a separate open trait may remain extensible.
cases.intended_cause: `Mine` can implement the open `Rule` contract, but it cannot satisfy the private prerequisite behind `BuiltIn`; the attempted privileged extension is therefore rejected.
cases.principled_repair: Implement the open execution trait or use a supported factory.
cases.weak_repair: Expose sealing internals publicly.
